title: BACH: Benchmarking Audio Codecs for Bio-Acoustic Health
abstract: Bio-acoustic health signals are increasingly vital for remote diagnostics, yet efficient transmission remains a bottleneck for clinical adoption. While audio codecs offer strong compression for general audio, they preserve diagnostically critical information in bio-acoustic signals is unclear. To address this gap, we introduce BACH, the first systematic Benchmark for evaluating Audio Codecs on bio-acoustic Health tasks. BACH assesses eight codecs across five bio-acoustic health tasks, utilizing a unified framework covering original audio, compressed representations, and reconstructed audio. Our central finding reveals a critical misalignment between reconstruction fidelity and downstream task performance: codecs excelling at signal reconstruction do not always retain task-relevant semantic cues. This highlights a fundamental challenge for future research: codecs for medical applications must be co-designed to optimize for both perceptual quality and diagnostic information preservation.
relevance_note: Benchmark of eight audio codecs on bio-acoustic health tasks. User decision at review (2026-11-01): rejected as out of scope (interesting, but not about generating or evaluating synthetic speech).
